speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) secondary to Chlamydia trachomatis or Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

The patient is a 17-year-old female with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and dysuria, accompanied by dyspareunia and inconsistent condom use. This clinical picture strongly suggests an ascending genital infection. I will immediately request a urine analysis and a sexually transmitted infection (STI) panel (NAAT for Chlamydia and Gonorrhea) to confirm the etiology and rule out other causes like appendicitis or pyelonephritis.
